newsitem.title: UK: Hyder unit to offer discounts on gas in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Hyder unit to offer discounts on gas in 1998.

text.p: British multi-utility Hyder Plc said on Tuesday its Swalec unit would offer gas to domestic customers at discounts of as much as 22 percent to Centrica, the domestic supply business of British Gas, when the market opens to competition.

"Swalec Gas is undercutting present British Gas prices by up to 22 percent -- the equivalent of 75 stg for an average UK customer -- and will be selling in north Wales as well as in the power company's stronghold of south Wales," a statement said.

Swalec, the regional electricity company (Rec) for south Wales bought by Welsh Water to form Hyder, said it was adding a sales force of 200 to sign up customers before 1998 when the domestic market opens up to competition.
"Today begins a new era of lower gas prices for Welsh customers. We will be the number one competitor to British Gas in Wales," Swalec chief executive John Roberts said.
Swalec is already selling gas to business customers throughout Britain and has sold to domestic customers in pilot schemes in Bristol and Avon in south western England.
Britain's domestic gas market is scheduled to open up to competition in 1998 along with a phased introduction of competition in the electricity market.
